title: Performance Comparison of Lump-Sum Design-Build (DB) and Progressive Design-Build (PDB) Methods in Infrastructure Projects
content: Progressive Design-Build (PDB) differs from traditional lump-sum Design-Build (DB) by allowing project design, scope, and cost to be progressively developed before the final construction price is established. However, empirical comparisons of these two delivery methods across infrastructure sectors remain limited. This study compares the performance of lump-sum DB and PDB projects in the transportation, water/wastewater, and aviation sectors using data obtained from the Design-Build Institute of America database. After data screening, the final sample consisted of 95 lump-sum DB and 37 PDB projects. We evaluated cost growth, schedule growth, and construction intensity using descriptive statistics and nonparametric statistical tests. PDB projects exhibited significantly lower mean cost growth than lump-sum DB projects (1.76% vs. 3.24%, respectively; p = 0.006). Construction intensity was also significantly lower for PDB projects ($141K/day) than for lump-sum DB projects ($358K/day) (p < 0.001). No statistically significant difference was found in schedule growth (p = 0.131). Overall, the findings suggest that PDB may offer improved cost control while maintaining schedule performance comparable to lump-sum DB for infrastructure projects.
